steps.text: Place spinach, basil, pine nuts, Parmesan cheese, 2 tablespoons olive oil, garlic, lemon juice, salt, lemon zest, and pepper into a food processor; blend until nearly smooth, scraping the sides of the bowl with a spatula as necessary.
Drizzle in remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil while processing until smooth.

raw_recipe.headline: Spinach Basil Pesto
raw_recipe.description: This tasty spinach pesto is easy to make by blending fresh spinach and basil with lemon juice, lemon zest, garlic, olive oil, and Parmesan cheese.

video.description: In this video, you’ll see how to make a super-simple pesto sauce, starring fresh baby spinach and basil. It freezes great for quick-and-easy weeknight meals. Enjoy it with pasta, use it to top pizzas, or serve it as a sauce with grilled meats or a garnish for soups.

review.reviewBody: How delicious! I have never made pesto sauce before, so this was my first attempt and it was exquisite! Finding at the last minute that I did not have pine nuts, I looked up on the internet to find a suitable substitute, and finding almonds were appropriate (and I had them) I used almonds. They cut up beautifully in the food processor and I have some left over which I am going to freeze for another treat some summer evening! I highly recommend it!

This is a fantastic recipe. The ingredients you choose make a difference- I make it with fresh ingredients as much as possible: fresh baby spinach, fresh basil, fresh lemon, real parmesan cheese, high quality EVOO. The only change I do regularly is to saute the garlic in some of the oil until it's golden brown before adding it as I find the raw garlic to be a bit strong. I've substituted sliced almonds for the pine nuts in a pinch and it's good (pine nuts are better, but honestly not sure it's enough to pay the premium in price!) Either way, be sure to toast them before adding them to the blender. This recipe is definitely a keeper!

We thought it was really good. I added more basil than it called for. I used a tad less salt and it was not too salty but I was worried about that. I used course Kosher salt. I toasted the pine nuts first in a pan. I may have used a little bit less of fresh garlic and I thought it was pretty strong. I usually use jarred garlic which I think is not as strong. I only have a small chopper but it was fine.
I made it again and made a lot more of it. I didn't use spinach this time and not sure if I should pat down the basil in the cup to measure it. I used 2+ packed down cups this time and upped up all the ingredients. I also added in some other greens like lemon leaves and arugula in some of my batches.

A really great pesto recipe!! We have nut allergies in our house so I wasn’t sure how to replace that component of the recipe. My mom suggested we bake a head of garlic (sprinkle some olive oil and salt on top) at 350 F for 1 hour. Replace with this garlic, add an extra clove than what the recipe calls, and it did the trick! Not an exact pesto flavor but the roasted garlic adds more of a nutty flavor than if you left them out altogether. Still was super delicious and perfect for the WHOLE family to enjoy!

This recipe is really easy, used the food processor, it was great! Added the parmesan during processing, did not want to wait & add it later. I have tried this with processed grated parmesan & parmesan reggiano fresh grated, it works well both ways. It stuck to the ice cube tray will not do that again. But I lined a mini muffin tin with plastic wrap, froze pucks & they popped right out with ease.

Good base recipe, and the lemon and lemon zest are nice touches. I tasted as I went along and so adapted it: I used at least 1/2 cup more basil; I stopped both nuts and cheese at no more than 1/3 cup each; and I used toasted walnuts instead of pine nuts (mostly because of the cost). My garlic cloves were large, and it was definitely strongly garlicky, which is fine with me. Personal preference: I always reduce the EVOO significantly (here to 2 tbs) and use broth for the difference, just because I find standard pesto too oily. Note: with my changes, this made a little over a cup—even with a few tablespoons more each of cheese and nuts, it would only be about 1-1/2 cups, which is more like 12 servings in my household. Also, someone said a blender doesn’t work, but I used mine and it was fine.

I started making this years ago and my wife loves it! She uses it on everything from steamed vegetables to meats to pasta. I never learned how to measure cups of greens, so I use a whole container of baby spinach, 5 containers of fresh basil, the zest and juice of a whole lemon, a whole bag of toasted pine nuts, a whole head of garlic, 1 tsp of salt and pepper and 4 tbls olive oil. I don’t add the Parmesan cheese cause it makes it too salty. Purée all of it and put it into ice cube trays and freeze. It will last +1 yr in a zip lock bag and it yields 19-20 cubes, good for 10-15 meals.

I followed the recipe exactly, except that I adjusted it for 60 servings for my freezer. I screwed up by using 1.5-TBSP, of kosher pink salt instead of teaspoons. OOps. I filed 3-500ml mason jars + another 250ml jar for my fridge. It is delicious. I love the combo of spinach + Basil leaves. Tip...pulse the nuts in the processor first before adding the other ingredients. Use a thinner viscosity olive oil, designed for salads, as it is lighter & less dense. Also do add the zest of lemon, as it makes a difference.

SO good!! I also substituted walnuts for pine nuts. Makes a good amount of vibrant bright green pesto. Beautiful and yummy! I mixed the pesto with the pasta and served with sliced smoked lemon pepper chicken breast, 10 out of 10 👌

Great recipe! I always make pesto this time of year and really enjoy putting it on almost everything. With this year's batch of basil I added 1 1/2 cups spinach and a lot more garlic. Thanks again for a great keeper! Debbie

I began making traditional pesto years ago. As time has gone by I’ve enjoy mixing the greens that I have on hand - homegrown basil, arugula & spinach. I go easy on the garlic and use lightly toasted walnuts and vegan Parmesan cheese. Can hardly go wrong! Great quick weeknight dinner.
I actually make a big batch of pesto and put it in the refrigerator to allow the flavor to marry and I totally loving it!, certainly make it again!
No changes. I froze it in ice cube trays to use in almost anything.

This is the best pesto. I've been making it for years! I'm allergic to pine nuts, so I use walnuts. My sister messaged me out of the blue saying she was craving "my" pesto - I don't even remember making it for her! When my son was 4, I made this for dinner. He stopped eating to look at me and say "this is a goooood green noodles, mama!" What else can I say about it? :)

This is much better than pesto with only basil. It mellows out the bitterness from the basil and adds a hint of sweetness. I have been making my own pesto for years and this was, by far, my best batch!

We made this today and put it over bow tie pasta and a small amount of wilted spinach. I didn't have pine nuts, but used Costco roasted almonds with sea salt. My garlic cloves were very large, so I only used 2. There was plenty of garlic flavor. We will be making this again.

Added another 1 c of basil leaves to balance the saltiness. Recommend the toasted pine nuts as it comes out with a really nutty flavor and would recommend reducing the 1/2 t kosher salt if you like to add your own. Makes about 1 cup in the single batch. Excellent flavor!
what are pine nuts? I was gonna make but now I don't want to. do they come from a pine tree? still a great meal yummers! old gramps loved it!
